messages:
Maya: Heads-up — multiple hosted API customers started seeing 502/504s ~02:07 UTC immediately after the maintenance window ended. Repro curl + example trace below. Raising here to triage.
infra-bot: maintenance window completed: rolling nginx + envoy restarts 01:58-02:05 UTC (change-id: mw-2026-03-18).
Ben: How widespread? percent of requests and which regions?
Maya: ~4-7% of requests in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 during the spike. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. Customer reports: intermittent 502 then successful retry.
Loren: I pulled proxy logs — lots of upstream resets to auth-service and midproxy. Snippet: 
```
[02:07:12] edge-proxy: upstream_reset: reason=connection_failure, upstream=auth-service, trace=tr-8a9f
[02:07:12] envoy: response_code=502, x-envoy-upstream-service-time=0
```
Olivia: Any recent config changes besides the maintenance restarts?
Maya: We pushed keepalive tuning + http2 settings during the window (tcp_keepalive_time reduced, http2_max_concurrent_streams increased). Change-ids: keepalive-2026-03 and h2-tune-02.
Ben: That aligns. If keepalive time was lowered we can see connection churn causing upstream pools to exhaust. Can someone paste the raw client headers for a failing request?
Maya: pasted sample request/response below: 
```
> curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/2 502
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 02:07:13 GMT
content-type: text/plain
content-length: 11
via: 1.1 envoy
x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 0

Bad Gateway
```
Jordan-CS: Customer reported volume of 120 req/s from their app during the time window, fronted by streaming calls. They saw ~10% failures, mostly on short streams.
Loren: I also grabbed an upstream tcpdump around 02:06:50 — I see lots of FIN/RESET between edge and auth (auth closed early). Hypothesis: auth-service health/probe flapping after restart caused rapid connection closure -> envoy treated as upstream failure -> 502.
Ben: Two actionable checks: 1) auth-service healthchecks & restart logs 2) edge proxy connection pool saturation metrics (active conns, queued). Can infra share auth pod logs?
infra-bot: auth-service pods restarted during window: pod/auth-7f9 crashed/restarted 02:03:10 (OOMKilled), readiness toggled until 02:10:40. Log head: 
```
panic: runtime: out of memory
...
```
Olivia: Ok that explains origin. OOM on auth during the window + aggressive keepalive/h2 changes -> connection churn. For immediate mitigation: 1) revert keepalive-2026-03 change (undo reduce) 2) add 1-minute autoscaling buffer on auth pods 3) temporarily extend healthcheck grace for auth.
Maya: Will communicate mitigations to CS and affected customers. Jordan-CS: can you do a customer-facing note?
Jordan-CS: Yep — I'll post an incident update to the customers and open a support ticket. ETA on revert?
Ben: Revert done (rolled back keepalive-2026-03 at 02:20). Edge proxies are now stable in metrics. I'll keep watch for 15m.
Loren: Follow-up: we should add circuit-breaker backoff for upstream auth to avoid thundering restarts, and tune http2 stream limits to avoid hot-path hits for embedding batches.
Maya: Repro steps (for eng): 
1) Start a steady stream of small streaming requests to /v1/generate at 100 rps.
2) Restart auth pods (kill to cause OOM-like restart).
3) Observe edge: 2-10% 502s during pod recovery, x-envoy-upstream-service-time=0.
Trace IDs: tr-8a9f, tr-8ad0 for two examples.

Ben: Thanks — I've opened infra ticket INFRA-2248 to track root cause + config rollback validation. Actions: rollback applied (done), add auth pod buffer, add probe grace, postmortem to follow.
OpsBot: Scheduled monitor: edge-upstream-502-rate, threshold 1%/5m. Notification to #oncall if >1% for 5m.
Maya: Closing loop with customers now. Will add short postmortem draft after we confirm no recurrence. :white_check_mark:
